skill.name: cohesivity
skill.description: Provision and operate Cohesivity backend services through MCP tools and authenticated HTTP APIs, with explicit approval for state changes, billing, and durable resources.
skill.summary: Build and operate Cohesivity infrastructure with guarded provisioning, server-side API access, lifecycle management, and billing controls.
skill.author: cohesivity-org

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are Markdown false positives. Two findings direct a version-pinned npx installer, while network access and local credential reuse are core behavior. Mutable live documentation can change operational instructions after marketplace review, creating a high-confidence remote instruction supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: Mutable remote documentation can change agent behavior after marketplace review.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle versioned operational documentation or verify fetched documents against audited hashes before following instructions.

remediation.issue: The fallback runs downloaded npm package code with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require separate execution approval and verify package provenance, integrity, and publisher identity before running the installer.

remediation.issue: The application key is placed in data-plane URL query parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Move credentials to authorization headers and redact query strings from logs, telemetry, and error reports.

remediation.issue: The service receives an attributing User-Agent from installers and manual clients.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact identity fields, retention policy, purpose, and available opt-out controls.

content.value_statement: Building an application often requires coordinating many backend providers, credentials, and consoles. This skill provisions Cohesivity services through one guarded workflow and API.
actual_capabilities: Creates or reuses Cohesivity project tenants through MCP tools or a version-pinned initializer.
Provisions databases, storage, hosting, authentication, realtime, email, browser, and AI API resources.
Guides authenticated server-side calls to Cohesivity control-plane and data-plane endpoints.
Manages tenant status, claiming, billing, and upgrades behind explicit approval gates.
Uses live resource documentation to obtain current endpoints, limits, pricing, and operational requirements.
Keeps management and application keys outside browser, mobile, and client-side bundles.
limitations: Requires network access to Cohesivity and may require an available Cohesivity MCP integration.
Fresh tenants expire after 72 hours and have strict resource caps until claimed.
Current APIs, limits, and pricing depend on mutable remote documentation.
Durable state, paid actions, upgrades, and managed agents require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Launch an Application Backend
use_cases.description: Provision a database, authentication, storage, and hosting for a new application without managing separate provider consoles.

use_cases.title: Add Managed Services
use_cases.description: Attach Redis, realtime messaging, email, vector storage, or model APIs to an existing project.

use_cases.title: Operate Project Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Check tenant status, review quotas, claim temporary projects, and perform approved billing actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Cohesivity backend for my project with Postgres and authentication. Explain the proposed tenant change and wait for required approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs basic backend services for a new application.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Managed Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project for an existing Cohesivity configuration. Add Redis using current service documentation and request approval before provisioning.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project needs one additional managed resource.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Server Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this server application for Cohesivity hosting. Review deployment files, protect secrets, show expected costs, and request approval before upload.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to deploy an existing server application.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Service Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cohesivity architecture using Postgres, vector storage, inbox, realtime, and an AI gateway. Verify live limits and stage every mutation for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced project needs coordinated infrastructure and controlled provisioning.

output_examples.input: Add a database and login to this notes application using Cohesivity.
output_examples.output: Found no existing tenant. Proposed resources: Postgres and social login. Tenant creation and each resource require approval before provisioning.

output_examples.input: Check whether this temporary project is close to its limits.
output: Tenant lifecycle: ephemeral, with 31 hours remaining.
Postgres usage is within its cap.
Browser minutes are near the shared identity limit.

output_examples.input: Deploy this API and keep it online after the trial ends.
output_examples.output: Deployment files are prepared, but claiming creates durable state. Current pricing must be reviewed before requesting claim and deployment approval.

best_practices: Reuse an existing valid tenant and read credentials only from the protected project configuration.
Fetch current resource documentation, summarize the planned effect, and obtain explicit authorization before every mutation.
Keep all Cohesivity keys server-side and redact them from logs, screenshots, chat, and deployment output.
anti_patterns: Do not create duplicate tenants when a valid project configuration or MCP tenant already exists.
Do not send direct control-plane mutations that bypass MCP confirmation checks.
Do not retry non-idempotent top-ups or cross billing and durable-state gates without explicit approval.

faq.question: What services can this skill provision?
faq.answer: It covers databases, caching, storage, hosting, authentication, realtime, inbox, browser automation, and selected AI APIs.

faq.question: Does tenant creation require approval?
faq.answer: Yes. Creating a tenant changes external state, so the current request must explicitly authorize it.

faq.question: Where are Cohesivity credentials stored?
faq.answer: Local project credentials reside in the .cohesivity file. Remote account credentials remain inside the account MCP.

faq.question: Can Cohesivity keys be used in browser code?
faq.answer: No. Management and application keys must remain server-side, with a proxy used for browser-only applications.

faq.question: How long does a new tenant last?
faq.answer: An ephemeral tenant lasts 72 hours and has resource caps. Claiming preserves it after explicit approval.

faq.question: Does the skill perform paid actions automatically?
faq.answer: No. Billing, upgrades, managed agents, and other paid actions require current pricing disclosure and explicit approval.
